engine.name: sglang

description: Live Pop!_OS deployment (container glm-5.3-flash-sglang-sm120) using the exact-docker bundle with six SM120 patches baked in (glm5_next model, deepseek_nextn MTP draft, quantization utils + modelopt quant, flash_mla_sm120 kernel, dsa_backend). Six 93 GB schedulers across the four GPUs (mem-fraction-static 0.90). MoE runner is flashinfer_cutlass because FlashInfer CuteDSL MoE only supports datacenter Blackwell majors [10].

traces.detail: --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl: RuntimeError 'No supported CUDA architectures found for major versions [10]' from flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/moe_utils.py::_get_moe_utils_module during CuteDslMoEWrapper::run::Swiglu autotune; weights and KV allocation had succeeded.

--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass: full load, KV cache fp8_e4m3 3,789,184 tokens per rank (25.62 GiB + 2.33 GiB), NEXTN target-verify CUDA graphs captured for bs [1..8] at num_tokens_per_req=6, 'The server is fired up and ready to roll!', GET /health -> 200.
temp=0 max_tokens=120: reasoning_content clean (verified 17x23 by decomposition), content 'Hello! 17 times 23 equals 391.', finish_reason=stop, 101 completion tokens incl. 88 reasoning tokens.
temp=1.0 top_p=0.95, chat_template_kwargs {reasoning_effort:'low'}, no max_tokens cap: FP8-vs-BF16-KV-cache question answered in clean markdown headings/bullets.
Default (max) reasoning effort, no max_tokens cap: projectile-motion quadratic solved symbolically with LaTeX, t = 2+sqrt(13) = 5.61 s, correct; reasoning/content split via glm45 parser.

Requests capped at max_tokens 120-900 under default (max) thinking effort all ended finish_reason=length with empty content field: budget consumed inside <think>. Chat template takes reasoning_effort ('low'|'high'; unset => 'max') and clear_thinking; there is no 'thinking': false kwarg.

Deployment handed to Local Studio: compose launch replaced by foreground wrapper launch-studio.sh; controller instance 'llm' state=ready; stale persisted instance record removed after controller restart. Proxy /v1/chat/completions routes model glm-5.3-flash correctly.

pi 0.84.3 (--provider homelab --model glm-5.3-flash) returned exact probe 'pi-e2e-ok'; omp 18.0.6 default role resolved to homelab/glm-5.3-flash and answered. Root cause of prior client failures: a single invalid 'video' input token in pi models.json zai entry made pi drop ALL custom providers.
9-run sweep: concurrency ladder (1/2/4/8 at low effort, 512-token cap), effort ladder (low/high/max at 1024 cap), 2x 5k-token prefill TTFT. Results in benchmarks block; raw JSON saved on host.

mem-fraction-static 0.90->0.93 (KV 3,789,184->4,087,680 tokens/rank); --enable-multimodal + chat-template override emitting real media markers. Vision verified: solid-red PNG answered 'Red'; video verified: 2s solid-blue MP4 answered 'Blue'. Prior blindness root cause: shipped chat_template.jinja is text-only (renders '<reminder>You are unable to process this image...'), so <|image|> spans never entered the prompt.

MTP geometry A/B on identical probes: draft=4 worse (138 solo / ~63 per-stream at 8-way vs 142/72 at draft=6); steps=6/draft=7 rejected by engine (NEXTN head depth cap). Kept 5/6. Accept rate improved 0.39-0.49 -> 0.60-0.68 (accept len 2.8-3.0). Sustained uncapped single-stream: 158-182 tok/s (16.3k-token deep probe at 158.6; earlier shorter prose peaked 207.6). Aggregate 8-way ~550 tok/s. NVFP4 KV cache explored: NOT available - kv-cache-dtype choices are auto/fp8_e5m2/fp8_e4m3/bf16 and dsa_backend hard-asserts fp8_e4m3.

benchmarks.methodology: OpenAI streaming API against engine port 8000 directly on pop-os (no proxy hop); temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95; fixed technical-essay prompt; max_tokens cap equalizes decode length for the sweep (benchmarking only - server imposes no cap); token counts from usage in final SSE chunk; aggregate tok/s = total completion tokens / batch wall time. Raw results: glm53-flash-deploy/sweep-20260826.json on pop-os.

prefill_5k_token_prompt.note: scheduler logs show 6.4k-18.9k tok/s prefill across mixed workloads

mtp_nextn5.note: NEXTN 5-step drafting; per-request variance by task type

benchmarks.scaling_note: Aggregate decode scales ~3.9x from 1 to 8 streams (142->550 tok/s) at low effort; per-stream degrades gracefully to ~70 tok/s at 8-way. Effort level barely changes decode tok/s (154->169 low->max); it changes how many of the generated tokens are hidden reasoning vs visible content.
benchmarks.prefill_note: Unique random corpora, chunked-prefill 8192, max-prefill-tokens 8192; prefill tok/s = prompt_tokens/TTFT (includes tokenize+queue). Holds ~6k tok/s flat to 100k tokens, mild drop at 213k. Earlier 'prefill_5k_token_prompt' entry superseded (its 0.13s warm case was a prefix-cache artifact of a repeated identical prompt).
